Date/time: 26 Jan 2025 1200 (ship's time UTC)

Master MV TORMAR SPRING

result.result:
The Master's ETA of 2025-01-31T11:00:00Z is consistent: check_eta computes 2025-01-31T12:18:00Z from the 1503.8 nm distance to go at 12.5 kn, a difference of only 1.3 hours (within the 2-hour tolerance). No charter party ETA notice is due: the last notice was sent at 5 days before arrival (2025-01-25), and the next notice point (3 days) has not yet been reached at 4.96 days to ETA. Notice recipients under the CP are the agent.

The report's main engine stop (06:10–11:40 UTC on 26 Jan) agrees with the report per check_stoppage: the reported speed over the 18.5 steaming hours reproduces the 231.3 nm distance run exactly, and the stop falls within the report day. The stoppage explanation (fuel oil filters choked with sludge, cleaned, engine restarted) needs no query to the Master.

Applying the CP off-hire clause — loss of time from breakdown of machinery or equipment is off hire — this stop is off hire. The simulated off-hire statement from the voyage management system (figures are made up for this simulation) gives: hire deducted $2,177.08 for 5.5 hours at $9,500/day, VLSFO 1.1 t at $660 (owners' account), total $2,837.08, for 2025-01-26T06:10:00Z to 2025-01-26T11:40:00Z. Caveat: because the choke may lie in fuel supplied by the charterers, the owner may argue responsibility — that claim is the operator's to make.

The operator should decide whether to put the ship off hire for 2025-01-26T06:10:00Z–2025-01-26T11:40:00Z and notify the owner (Tormar Bulk Carriers). On a yes: (a) propose a voyage management system off-hire entry for that period, and (b) e-mail the owner's vessel technical management giving the period and reason (fuel oil filters choked with sludge) and asking for the engine log extract for the stop.

Dear Operations,

We report that MV TORMAR SPRING was put off hire for a main-engine stoppage on 26 Jan 2025 from 06:10 to 11:40 UTC (5.5 hours).

Reason per voyage_agent: fuel oil filters choked with sludge stirred up in heavy weather. Filters were cleaned, the engine restarted, and the vessel resumed passage.

VLSFO used during the stoppage: 1.1 t (generators and boiler), for owners' account per the charter party.

Please provide the engine log extract for the stop.

Regards,
Operations
